market_holds: Spot 103.41 at the 18:08 UTC seal (sealed baseline), after a +17% session that only tracked the AI-connectivity group: SOXX +13.5%, CRDO +21%, ALAB +20%, MTSI +17%, COHR +15%. Several of them opened higher and gave some of it back during the day (Yahoo daily bars, pulled 19:19 UTC). Before today SMTC fell from 146.97 (Oct 28) to 87.63 (Nov 20). Over the same span ALAB fell about 39%, CRDO 43% and MRVL 52%, so the drawdown is sector beta and not anything specific to Semtech. Run-up is -24.4% over 20 days, and the stock is -47.6% from its 52-week high of about 202 (Oct 2). Options to Nov 27: the straddle prices 13.5% (event-net 5.3% in the baseline), 25-delta skew is +16.7 vol points (downside paid) and put/call open interest is 0.21 (call-heavy). Short interest was 7.49M shares at 10/30, up from 6.02M at 10/15, 2.5 days to cover (Nasdaq). Q3 is effectively pre-announced. The Oct 15 8-K narrowed the guide to $417.5M +/- $2.5M revenue, 59.0% adjusted gross margin, 33.0% +/- 10bp adjusted operating margin and $1.14 +/- $0.02 EPS, about ten days before quarter end. Published consensus is around $416M / $1.13 (Earnings Whispers preview, Nov 15), and the Nasdaq/Zacks feed is visibly stale at $0.92 for Oct and $1.07 for Jan. So the quarter holds almost no surprise. What is left is the Jan-quarter guide (with the Compal cellular-module sale due to close in FQ4, worth $48.1M of revenue in Q2) and what management says about FY28 bookings and capacity. Prior reactions in the baseline: +10.4% (Aug, guide 8% above consensus), -4.4% (May), -11% (Mar, in line with a modest guide), +2.5%, +15.1%, -4.6%, +21.1%.
view: The quarter itself is not the event. Management narrowed the guide to +/- $2.5M about ten days before the quarter closed, so revenue near $418-422M and EPS near $1.15-1.16 is the base case and close to consensus. The reaction turns on the Jan-quarter guide, plus whatever management says about FY28 bookings (over 70% booked as of the Aug call) and capacity (the Tower SiGe deal of Oct 13). Fundamentals look intact. Data center was guided +45% q/q for Q3. Innolight's Q3 showed 1.6T revenue growth accelerating. Nvidia beat on Nov 17 and guided its Q4 to $130B against about $125B expected. Coherent's print in this same fragile tape was followed by an +18% day. Semtech has guided above consensus in three of its last four quarters. Against that, the stock now trades as a high-beta AI-connectivity proxy. It fell with the group and bounced 17% with the group today, so a large part of the scored window (today's close to tomorrow's open) is the sector's overnight move, and I cannot predict that. Two specific risks to the guide: the cellular divestiture could make the Jan-quarter revenue guide look flat or down against estimates that still carry that business, and AAOI's Q3 call named 1.6T DSP supply as the immediate constraint on module builds. The Oct 15 analyst day also showed that 'raised but not spectacular' gets sold in this tape (-10% that day). On balance I lean modestly up: after a roughly 45% de-rating, a clean beat-and-raise with confirmation on FY28 should get a relief bid. But the lean does not clear the bar for a call.
unpriced: Possibly the gap between a fundamental story the company has re-confirmed recently (Q3 pre-raised, FY30 EPS framework of $12.40-13.00 against a stock near 8x that) and a price that de-rated purely on sector macro (midterm data-center worries, the Nvidia CEO exit, financing fears). I cannot show that a beat-and-raise is unpriced, because the 13.5% straddle and the sector beta can absorb it, so I make no claim.

recommendation.reason: Q3 was pre-announced with a +/- $2.5M range, so the release mostly turns on the Jan-quarter guide and FY28 commentary. Both lean positive on counterparty evidence (Innolight 1.6T acceleration, Nvidia's guide, the company's habit of guiding above consensus), but the cellular divestiture and DSP supply are real downside risks to the headline guide. The window is overnight in a stock moving 10-17% a day with its sector, so sector beta swamps a modest idiosyncratic edge. 57% does not meet the 65% bar.
recommendation.what_would_flip_it: A Jan-quarter revenue guide that excludes the cellular module business and lands below a consensus still carrying it, or any comment that 1.6T DSP or capacity limits cap data-center growth. Either would make this a down reaction. A guide well above ~$430M with data center up more than 20% q/q would push p_up toward 65.

self_critique: The strongest case against a modest-up lean: the Oct 15 analyst day showed this stock gets sold on 'good but expected', and every company-specific positive (Q3 raise, FY30 framework, 70% booked) is already public and repeated in previews. Today's +17% sector squeeze may already have pulled forward any relief, and the intraday fade across peers suggests supply on strength. A divestiture-adjusted Q4 guide could easily print below a consensus that still carries the cellular business, and the put skew says the options market fears exactly that. The opposite case is just as plausible: after a 45% de-rating, any confirmation could squeeze shorts, which rose to 7.5M shares. The two roughly cancel, which is why I stay near 55-57.
approach_notes: P4 (priced is a claim to prove) and the freshest-data-first rule paid: the Oct 15 8-K showed that Q3 is pre-announced, which moved the whole question to the Q4 guide. P6 helped name the line. Neither the playbook nor the baseline handles a name whose window is dominated by sector beta; a step to measure the share of recent moves explained by the peer group would have saved time.
